A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Panda research work. The text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–N support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting, completion, ablation, scaling, and attractor-statistics experiments on synthetic chaotic systems, experimental recordings, and PDE simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional baseline comparisons, completion results, dataset analyses, and long-horizon failure measurements.

M1.justification: The evolutionary data-generation procedure, dynamics embeddings, temporal/channel attention, and forecasting/MLM objectives are retained. The new 66M MLM checkpoint scales the existing architecture. Expanded residual-block and pooling descriptions do not establish a changed method; optimizer and training-budget revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic founder/skew-product ODEs, double-pendulum recordings, eigenworms, electronic circuits, Kuramoto–Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex-street PDEs, and masked completion. Added analyses and longer evaluations reuse this coverage; changes concern configurations, sample counts, and procedures.

E2.justification: v3 adds DynaMix to ODE forecasting and long-horizon comparisons, FNO and DeepONet to PDE evaluation, and cubic-spline, linear, and degree-3 polynomial interpolation to completion. Figure 2 replaces Chronos 20M with Chronos 200M, previously evaluated elsewhere. Long-horizon comparisons also replace probabilistic Chronos variants with an expanded deterministic comparator set.

E3.justification: Long-term evaluation changes from 128–512-step forecasts using full-trajectory or context-inclusive references to 512–3584-step, horizon-matched evaluations and tail-only scoring. Completion evaluation changes from 3584 to 4096 points and adds the 66M checkpoint; operator-baseline training introduces additional PDE protocols. Appendix B revises Adam to AdamW and Chronos-SFT settings from batch 128 and ten times Panda's iterations to batch 160 and 300K iterations. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a tsfresh/UMAP analysis of founder–offspring diversity. Appendix F adds KL-estimator sensitivity and tail-only mean-regression tests, replacing shorter-horizon Lyapunov correlation tables with longer-horizon distribution comparisons. Appendix N adds spline-versus-Panda case studies. The attention-resonance and patch-length analyses already existed and are not new experiments.

E5.justification: Completion evaluation changes its reported averaging from five independent masks in v2 Figure 15 to eight seeded masks in v3 Figure 18/Table 10, alongside changed model/context settings. v3 also documents Monte Carlo KL estimation. Mean/standard-deviation, interquartile-range, and Holm–Šidák-adjusted Wilcoxon reporting remain established practices.

E6.justification: Many original short-horizon table values remain, but substantial results are added or replaced. v3 Table 17 reports tail-only KL divergence of 15.25 for Panda, 7.00 for Chronos 20M SFT, and 3.50 for DynaMix. Table 10 adds completion R² values of 0.91 for Panda MLM-66M, 0.78 for Panda MLM, and 0.71 for cubic splines. Table 6 adds a nonsignificant 512-step sMAPE comparison against probabilistic Chronos 20M SFT (p=0.326). These are new evaluations, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds an explicit local-bandwidth objective and Gaussian-mixture/Monte Carlo construction for KL estimation, beyond v2's brief metric description. The skew-product equations, correlation-dimension derivation, and spatiotemporal-attention derivation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset-generation, zero-shot forecasting, diversity-scaling, and ODE-to-PDE contributions remain. The abstract replaces explicit preservation of 'long-term statistics' with preservation of 'distributional measures' and elevates the already-reported resonance and experimental-data findings into its headline description.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledged mean regression while emphasizing consistent distributional advantages. v3 explains where Chronos-SFT and DynaMix outperform Panda, discusses failures for large Lyapunov exponents, and connects parroting to unstable periodic orbits. It adds substantive qualifications about DynaMix's preferred context length and the operator baselines' one-step settings, limiting interpretation of those comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendices B, F, H, and K add architecture tables, residual-block operations, KL pseudocode, operator-baseline configurations, training times, and MLM-66M training details. Section 8 consolidates code/checkpoint access and adds the 66M checkpoint pointer. However, v2's direct links to both training datasets and the smaller MLM checkpoint are absent from v3; this does not establish that those resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning relative to DynaMix and Almost-Linear RNNs, plus citations supporting parroting, periodic orbits, tsfresh/UMAP, and operator-learning implementations. References to Kloeden–Kozyakin and structured state-space models are removed. The main distinction based on evolutionary data generation and multivariate forecasting remains.

P1.justification: The long-term section is rewritten and moved from Section 5.4 to 5.6. Appendix G's resonance and attention-map discussion becomes main-text Section 5.5, while Appendix F is reorganized into six subsections. New acknowledgements and reproducibility sections and substantial appendix restructuring change the narrative beyond routine copyediting.

P2.justification: v2's attention Figures 17–19 are recomposed as main-text Figures 7–8, and its separate main KL/Hellinger tables become a combined table. PDE Figure 6 is redrawn with additional baselines and clearer panels. New UMAP, long-horizon, and completion displays, architecture/configuration tables, and revised galleries substantially change presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 already recognized mean regression, but its long-term argument relied largely on 128–512-step forecasts. v3 tests up to 3584 steps, checks alternative KL estimation, and isolates forecast tails, substantially improving evidence about where preservation fails. Added comparators and implementation details strengthen validation and reproducibility. Unequal comparison settings, retained blanket significance wording contradicted by Table 6, and removed dataset links are drawbacks, but the substantially more informative assessment of Panda's capabilities and limits outweighs them.
